facts.value: This online MSc in Engineering Practice is designed to support you in producing a significant, practice-focused research thesis that delivers measurable impact within your organisation.

It emphasises collaboration both with your fellow learners across diverse industries while giving you the flexibility to build on your previous studies and apply them directly to real-world engineering challenges in your workplace.

The MSc is open to learners who have already completed two Professional Diplomas or 60 ECTS Credits at Level 9 in areas such as aviation, operations management, ICT, artificial intelligence, data analytics, supply chain, or regulatory affairs.
The programme also supports Recognised Prior Learning for applicants who may have only one Professional Diploma but have a minimum of 5 years relevant work experience.

This programme provides learners not only the opportunity to drive improvements in engineering practices but also gain opportunities to showcase and apply their research work across professional and industry settings.
Particularly suited to mid to senior managers and experienced professionals seeking to strengthen their expertise and broaden their influence within their organisation.

Biomedical engineering

Chemical engineering

Civil engineering

Engineers apply mathematics and the physical sciences to find novel solutions to problems or to improve existing solutions.
Engineers need proficient knowledge of relevant sciences for their design projects.
If multiple solutions exist, engineers weigh each design choice based on their merit and choose the solution that best matches the requirements.
The task of the engineer is to identify, understand, and interpret the constraints on a design in order to yield a successful result.
It is generally insufficient to build a technically successful product; it must also meet further requirements.

Constraints may include the fundamental laws of physics and chemistry, available resources, physical, imaginative or technical limitations, flexibility for future modifications and additions, and other factors such as requirements for cost, safety, marketability, productivity, and serviceability.
By understanding the constraints, engineers derive specifications for the limits within which a viable object or system may be produced and operated.
Computers and software play an increasingly important role in modern scientific and technological endeavors.
One of the most widely used design tools in the profession is computer-aided design (CAD) software.
CAD enables engineers to create 3D models, 2D drawings, and schematics of their designs.
CAD together with digital mockup (DMU) and CAE software allows engineers to create models of designs that can be analyzed without having to make expensive and time-consuming physical prototypes.

These allow products and components to be checked for flaws; assess fit and assembly; study ergonomics; and to analyze static and dynamic characteristics of systems such as stresses, temperatures, electromagnetic emissions, electrical currents and voltages, digital logic levels, fluid flows, and kinematics.
Access and distribution of information is generally organized with the use of product data management software.
There are many tools to support specific engineering tasks such as computer-aided manufacturing (CAM) software to generate CNC machining instructions.
Manufacturing process management software is used for production engineering.
EDA software is used for printed circuit board (PCB) and circuit schematics for electronic engineers.
MRO applications are used for maintenance management.
Architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) software is used for civil engineering.
The use of computer software to aid the development of goods has collectively come to be known as product lifecycle management (PLM).

Engineering is an important and learned profession. As members of this profession, engineers are expected to exhibit the highest standards of honesty and integrity. Engineering has a direct and vital impact on the quality of life for all people. Accordingly, the services provided by engineers require honesty, impartiality, fairness, and equity, and must be dedicated to the protection of the public health, safety, and welfare. Engineers must perform under a standard of professional behavior that requires adherence to the highest principles of ethical conduct.

facts.value: Business engineering deals with the relationship between professional engineering, IT systems, business administration and change management.
Engineering management, or 'Management engineering', is a specialized field of management concerned with engineering practice or the engineering industry sector.
The demand for management-focused engineers has resulted in the development of specialized engineering management degrees that develop the knowledge and skills needed for these roles.

During an engineering management course, students will develop industrial engineering skills, knowledge, and expertise, alongside knowledge of business administration, management techniques, and strategic thinking.
Engineers specializing in change management must have in-depth knowledge of the application of industrial and organizational psychology principles and methods.
Professional engineers often train as certified management consultants in the very specialized field of management consulting applied to engineering practice or the engineering sector.

This work often deals with large scale complex business transformation or business process management initiatives in various sectors including aerospace and defence, automotive, oil and gas, machinery, pharmaceutical, food and beverage, electrical and electronics, power distribution and generation, utilities, and transportation systems.

These initiatives are typically sponsored by C-level executives and require a combination of technical engineering practice, management consulting practice, industry sector knowledge, and change management expertise.

facts.value: Engineering is one of the most popular and dynamic fields of study in India, offering a wide range of specialisations across science and technology. It focuses on designing, developing, and maintaining systems, machines, and structures that improve everyday life. Engineering courses provide strong career opportunities in multiple industries worldwide.
To pursue an undergraduate engineering degree in India, students must complete their 10+2 in the Science stream from a recognised board.
For postgraduate courses, a bachelor’s degree in engineering with a minimum of 50 per cent marks is required.
Engineering graduates play a vital role in innovation and development, contributing to fields like information technology, electronics, civil infrastructure, mechanical design, and renewable energy.
With a growing demand for skilled engineers globally, pursuing an engineering course in India ensures excellent learning opportunities and rewarding career prospects.

facts.value: Electrical Engineers design, develop, and maintain electrical systems and equipment. They work on power generation, transmission, and distribution, ensuring efficiency and safety in electrical networks.
Software Engineers develop, test, and maintain software applications and systems. They work on programming, debugging, and implementing solutions for businesses and technology platforms.
Computer Engineers design and optimise computer hardware and software systems. They focus on networking, system architecture, and improving computing efficiency.
Aerospace Engineers design, develop, and test aircraft, spacecraft, and related systems. They work on aerodynamics, propulsion, and safety in aviation and space technologies.
Civil Engineers plan, design, and supervise construction projects such as buildings, roads, and bridges. They ensure structures are safe, sustainable, and comply with regulations.
Electronics Engineers design, develop, and maintain electronic circuits and devices. They work on communication systems, consumer electronics, and control systems.
Mechanical Engineers design, analyse, and maintain mechanical systems and machines. They work on engines, manufacturing equipment, and thermal systems.
Marine Engineers design, operate, and maintain ships and offshore structures. They ensure propulsion, power systems, and onboard machinery function efficiently.
Engineering graduates can work in various areas such as PSUs, the Private Sector, the Indian Armed Forces, and other Government Departments.
